name: ALT (Asian Language Treebank) Test — All Pairs
description: Multi-way parallel evaluation corpus from the Asian Language Treebank (NICT). 13 languages (Bengali, English, Filipino, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Khmer, Lao, Malay, Myanmar/Burmese, Thai, Vietnamese, Chinese), built from Wikinews articles and sentence-aligned across all languages. Champollion uses the official ALT-Standard TEST split (the 1,018 English sentences whose article URLs are listed in URL-test.txt); a few cells are absent where ALT never translated a sentence into a given language, so per-pair sizes vary slightly (1016-1018). Only the BARE PARALLEL corpus (CC-BY-4.0) is used — the per-language treebank annotation layers (CC-BY-NC-SA) are deliberately NOT ingested. Adds the SEA gap: Lao, Khmer, Burmese, Filipino, Malay.

segments.name: ALT-Standard Test
segments.purpose: MT evaluation — the official ALT-Standard test split (URL-test.txt), news domain

download.instructions: Download ALT-Parallel-Corpus-20191206.zip (the CC-BY-4.0 bare parallel corpus ONLY — not the CC-BY-NC-SA treebank layers) plus URL-test.txt from the same base URL. Members data_{code}.txt hold lines 'SNT.{urlid}.{sentid}\t{text}'; all languages are line-aligned by the SNT id. The ALT-Standard test split is the sentences whose {urlid} is in URL-test.txt. Legacy codes: data_bg.txt is BENGALI (not Bulgarian); data_en_tok.txt (tokenized English) is never used.

source.publisher: NICT (National Institute of Information and Communications Technology) / ALT Project
source.citation: Riza et al. (2016). Introduction of the Asian Language Treebank. O-COCOSDA 2016. Thu et al. (2016), LREC 2016 (Myanmar). Ding et al. (2018/2019) (Khmer/Lao).

license.aiTraining: Permitted with attribution under CC-BY-4.0 (parallel corpus only).
license.notes: Only the ALT parallel corpus is CC-BY-4.0. The per-language treebank annotation layers (English-ALT, Japanese-ALT, my-alt, km-nova) are CC-BY-NC-SA and are NOT used here.

usageRestrictions.communityNotes: Reserved as an evaluation benchmark within Champollion. doNotTrain protects benchmark integrity.

contamination.reasoning: ALT is built from Wikinews and has been publicly distributed since ~2016; it is a well-known parallel corpus and portions may appear in large web-crawled MT/LLM training sets. Lower contamination than FLORES+/NTREX for the rarer SEA target languages, but not newly hand-crafted.

_provenance.populatedFrom: ALT-Parallel-Corpus-20191206.zip + URL-test.txt from the NICT ALT page. Test-split size (1018) verified by direct line count; archive + split shas pinned.
